visualReview.freshViews: All five sources side/oblique/top source and candidate (30 screenshots); actual quarter-cycle burst motion Herring top, Picasso/Yellow oblique (12 screenshots); unified marine desktop/mobile and 390px final single fish.
findings: Full original body silhouettes, UV coloration and source fin contour detail retained in static reference/candidate views.
No obvious Picasso median fin/body root tearing or fragmented Herring dorsal/body patches in reviewed current phases.
Herring posterior wave crosses the tail smoothly with the anterior head stable; Yellow retains a steadier anterior body with posterior tail response.

Frozen candidate eyes intentionally differ from original source eyes; source ocular data, renderer/shader and head transport code unchanged after CRLF-to-LF normalization; exact seeded 30-second gaze states unchanged.
Blue-label source remains 512px and low polygon density; Colorful actual fish material is 128px. Current material support cannot create absent original detail.
Unified R14 viewport and five-species viewport appear one at a time; mobile fish and controls fit the viewport.
limitations: User visual acceptance and biological gait calibration remain pending.

Some very slender source triangles have relative area expansion up to 1.410 and contraction to 0.730 despite all measured edges remaining within 25 percent. This is recorded in full, not hidden as zero strain.
Picasso source filename does not verify species identity or a specific biological gait.
Complete embedded original fish sources make the standalone file about 98.7 MiB; GPU memory and 30-fish cost still depend on hardware.
